(a) people can categorize emotion words into discrete categories; (b) the categories they form have some degree of consistency across people and situations; (c) the categories they use have some relationship with the categories used by scientists; and (d) the categories they construct are not entirely independent of their own emotional experiences.
people experience emotions by categorizing instances of affective feeling in terms of emotion prototypes.

the nature and structure of emotions and the ways in which they are expressed.

emotions are not discrete events, but instead are experienced as instances of affective feeling, and that the experience of emotion occurs when an individual categorizes an affective feeling in terms of emotion concepts that are grounded in bodily experience.
emotion experience is an act of embodied conceptualization that is guided by a social cognitive process of categorization.

we are interested in the relationship between emotion, cognition, and behavior.
